age.explain: Estradiol and testosterone are cleared a little more slowly with age, so the same dose reads a little higher later in life: about 0.5 to 0.7% a year. Left blank, the estimate is as for a %1-year-old, the average age in the studies the model was fitted on. The evidence is firmer for testosterone than for estradiol, and blood tests correct the estradiol estimate either way. Cyproterone is not adjusted.
app.name: Oyama's HRT Tracker
cal.desc.ekf: Extended Kalman Filter. Walks your labs in time order, keeping a running estimate of personal amplitude and clearance with its uncertainty. Permanent memory — every lab leaves a mark.
cal.desc.forward: Causal — each point uses only the labs available by then, so past estimates never change when you add a new lab.
cal.desc.mipd: Model-informed precision dosing. MAP fit of amplitude and clearance under a population prior with a robust (Student-t) likelihood: leans on the population when labs are sparse and shrugs off a lone outlier.
cal.desc.off: No calibration — shows the raw pharmacokinetic model.
cal.desc.ou_kalman: Ornstein–Uhlenbeck Kalman smoother. Treats the correction as a level that drifts and reverts toward the model — each lab's pull fades over about two weeks. Tracks change over time rather than one fixed scale.
cal.desc.retrospective: Smoothed — all labs re-estimate the whole history. More accurate in hindsight; a new lab can revise older estimates.
cal.desktop_note: Lab results aren't in the desktop app yet, so the choice is kept for when they are and the curve shows the model as it is
